# E138 -- Friends With Benefits

## Metadata
- **Brand:** Friends With Benefits (FWB)
- **Industry:** Crypto / DAO / Web3 Social Club
- **Year:** 2021 (references "Miami 2021" and NFT auction dates in May 2021)
- **Source file:** c4a00945929b266cf9e329229f2e33eb.pdf
- **Designed by:** CTHDRL (Cathedral)
- **Version:** V1.1
- **Scope:** Brand guidelines covering logo elements, design system (color, effects, typography), and FWB.Gallery product components (~35 pages)

## Brand Strategy
- **Positioning tagline:** "Crypto -- Culture" / "We Are"
- **Nature:** A social DAO (Decentralized Autonomous Organization) at the intersection of crypto and culture
- **No formal strategy section:** The guidelines are almost entirely visual/product-focused with no documented mission, values, or positioning framework
- **Implied positioning:** Premium, culturally-aware crypto community; emphasis on art, music, and digital culture (NFT gallery as primary product showcase)

## Logo
- **Wordmark:** "FWB." with extensible system -- keep "FWB." prefix and change secondary word to match product or event (FWB.GALLERY, FWB.PRODUCT, FWB.HELP, FWB.MIAMI 2021)
- **Typeface basis:** Combination of Everett (grotesque sans) and Orpheus Pro (organic serif) with subtle letterform adjustments
- **Construction:** X-height shifted up; all characters adjusted to match; letters kerned to -5% for cohesion and legibility
- **Pill version:** Shorthand abbreviated form of the wordmark in a pill/capsule shape
- **Stacked version:** Available for vertical layouts
- **Mark:** A "W" character with bird-head forms -- the W's curves mimic bird heads (especially in the curve and terminal of the right ascender); serifs removed from middle ascender to blend grotesque and serif
- **Stretched state:** The mark has a default and stretched variant where the W can be horizontally extended
- **Do's and Don'ts:** Never isolate a single bird head (always show at least 2); only arms can be stretched/warped (not bodies); do not change underlying character design (colors/textures OK)
- **Color versions:** Black (#000000) and cream (#F8F2F2)

## Typography
- **Primary typeface:** TWK Everett (designed by Nolan Paparelli, 2021) -- modern symmetrical grotesque with playful tension in corners/curves; feels "born of the digital world" with graphic fluidity
- **Primary weights:** Regular, Medium, Bold
- **Secondary typeface:** Orpheus Pro Italic -- organic flowing serif used only to highlight specific words/phrases; provides counterbalance to Everett's rigidity
- **Balance principle:** The personality of the system comes from contrast between organic script and geometric sans-serif; neither should dominate
- **Type hierarchy:**
  - H1: Everett Medium, 90px, 90% line-height
  - H2: Orpheus Pro, 50px, 100% line-height
  - H3: Everett Medium, 30px, 95% line-height
  - H4: Everett Medium, 30px, 120% line-height
  - Detail: Everett Regular, 10px, 130% line-height
  - Body: Everett Regular, 14px, 120% line-height
- **Font settings:** Slashed zero mandatory; "One Display" alternate glyph for the numeral 1
- **Rules:** Headlines always in Everett and largest on page; Orpheus only for accent/quotes; Everett for all numbers; Everett for 100% of body copy

## Color
- **Primary palette (2 + spot):**
  - Primary Black: #000000
  - Primary Cream: #F8F2F2
  - Spot/Highlight color: pulled from accompanying artwork (variable; pink used as default example)
- **Usage:** Black as primary background; cream for typography and elements; scheme can be flipped (cream bg, black type)
- **Highlight color:** Used for CTAs and areas of interest; contextual and changes per application

## Graphics
- **The Glow effect:** Outer glow applied to objects and type for emphasis; glow color matches the highlight/spot color
- **Image Displacement:** After Effects technique using abstract stock video as displacement map source on artwork; detailed 4-step tutorial provided with specific AE settings
- **Organic NFTs:** 3D objects wrapped with NFT art; non-static, non-conforming approach
- **Line art:** Thin line work graphic elements in black and cream for content housing (cards, ticker bars, misc elements)
- **Visual philosophy:** Rigid grid structure as counterbalance to organic 3D NFTs and displacement maps

## Photography
- **No traditional photography guidelines** -- the visual system is built around digital art, NFT imagery, and video rather than photography
- **Imagery approach:** Full-screen imagery and video; auto-play or triggered by video player
- **NFT-centric:** Artwork showcased as primary visual content (e.g., Miley Cyrus "Dead Petz" album art as case study)

## Applications
- **FWB.Gallery:** Primary product application documented -- an NFT auction/gallery platform
- **Grid system:** Website divided into 3 equal columns, each with its own 12-column sub-grid
- **Component library:**
  - Place Bid button (primary CTA) -- filled default state, glow-only hover state
  - Secondary buttons and links (expand, text links with arrow notation "->", alt button icons)
  - Cards (bidder cards with ETH values, usernames)
  - Ticker bar
  - Video player with timestamp
  - Bid history and NFT details (edition, creator share percentage)
- **Spacing system:** Rigid component spacing creating structure to counterbalance organic 3D content

## Tone of Voice
- **No formal tone of voice section** documented in the guidelines
- **Implied tone:** Casual, culturally literate, crypto-native; uses Web3 terminology naturally (ETH, bids, drops, wallets); music and art references as cultural currency
- **UI copy style:** Minimal, functional, lowercase-leaning with arrow notation for links

## Outliers
- **Extensible wordmark system** -- "FWB." as a constant prefix with variable product/event suffix is an unusually flexible naming architecture
- **Bird-head W mark** -- the logomark embeds dual bird heads within the letter W; the "friendship" theme encoded in the "always show at least 2 heads" rule
- **After Effects displacement tutorial** -- unusually specific production technique embedded directly in brand guidelines
- **Crypto-native design system** -- built for Web3 context with ETH pricing, wallet addresses, and auction mechanics as first-class design elements
- **Variable spot color** -- the highlight/accent color intentionally changes per context rather than being fixed, allowing the brand to adapt to any artwork

## Quality Score
**3 / 5** -- A focused, aesthetically strong guide that captures the Web3/crypto-culture aesthetic effectively. The extensible wordmark system and typography pairing (Everett + Orpheus Pro) are well-considered. However, it lacks brand strategy foundations (no mission, values, or positioning), has no tone of voice section, and is narrowly scoped to one product (FWB.Gallery). The After Effects displacement tutorial is a nice production touch but feels more like a creative brief than brand guidelines. Several spelling errors throughout ("cohession," "puprose," "abliity," "occassion") suggest a v1 draft that could use editorial polish.
